en.q: A tuning fork is used to produce resonance in a glass tube. The length of the air column in this tube can be adjusted by a variable piston. At room temperature of 27 °C two successive resonances are produced at 20 cm and 73 cm of column length. If the frequency of the tuning fork is 320 Hz, the velocity of sound in air at 27 °C is :
en.sol:
Successive resonances in a closed tube are λ/2 apart: λ/2 = 73 − 20 = 53 cm ⇒ λ = 106 cm = 1.06 m. (Using the difference cancels the end correction.)

v = fλ = 320 × 1.06 = 339.2 m/s ≈ 339 m/s.
en.hint: Difference of successive resonance lengths = λ/2.

en.q: A student measured the diameter of a small steel ball using a screw gauge of least count 0.001 cm. The main scale reading is 5 mm and zero of circular scale division coincides with 25 divisions above the reference level. If screw gauge has a zero error of −0.004 cm, the correct diameter of the ball is :
en.sol:
Reading = main scale + circular scale × least count = 0.5 cm + 25 × 0.001 cm = 0.525 cm.

Corrected = reading − zero error = 0.525 − (−0.004) = 0.529 cm.
en.hint: Subtract the zero error with its sign.

en.q: A screw gauge has least count of 0.01 mm and there are 50 divisions in its circular scale. The pitch of the screw gauge is :
en.sol: Least count = pitch/number of circular divisions ⇒ pitch = 0.01 mm × 50 = 0.5 mm.

hi.q: एक स्क्रूगेज का अल्पतमांक 0.01 mm है और इसके वृत्तीय पैमाने पर 50 विभाजन हैं। स्क्रूगेज का चूड़ी अंतराल है :
hi.sol: अल्पतमांक = चूड़ी अंतराल/वृत्तीय विभाजनों की संख्या ⇒ चूड़ी अंतराल = 0.01 mm × 50 = 0.5 mm।

en.q:
A screw gauge gives the following readings when used to measure the diameter of a wire
Main scale reading : 0 mm
Circular scale reading : 52 divisions
Given that 1 mm on main scale corresponds to 100 divisions on the circular scale. The diameter of the wire from the above data is :
en.sol: Least count = 1 mm/100 = 0.01 mm. Diameter = 0 + 52 × 0.01 mm = 0.52 mm = 0.052 cm.

en.q: In a vernier callipers, (N + 1) divisions of vernier scale coincide with N divisions of main scale. If 1 MSD represents 0.1 mm, the vernier constant (in cm) is :
en.sol: (N + 1) VSD = N MSD ⇒ 1 VSD = N/(N + 1) MSD. Vernier constant = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = MSD/(N + 1) = 0.1 mm/(N + 1) = 0.01 cm/(N + 1) = 1/(100(N + 1)) cm.

hi.q: एक वर्नियर केलिपर्स में वर्नियर पैमाने के (N + 1) विभाजन, मुख्य पैमाने के N विभाजनों के संपाती होते हैं। यदि 1 MSD, 0.1 mm निरूपित करता है, तो वर्नियर नियतांक (cm में) है :
hi.sol: (N + 1) VSD = N MSD ⇒ 1 VSD = N/(N + 1) MSD। वर्नियर नियतांक = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = MSD/(N + 1) = 0.1 mm/(N + 1) = 0.01 cm/(N + 1) = 1/(100(N + 1)) cm।

en.q: Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier Scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at x = 0.1 cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed. If the main scale reading for the diameter is M = 5 cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is :
en.sol:
Least count = 1 M.S.D. − 1 V.S.D. = 0.1 − 0.09 = 0.01 cm. With the jaws closed the V.S. zero is at +0.1 cm: zero error = +0.1 cm.

Reading = 5 + 8 × 0.01 = 5.08 cm. Corrected diameter = 5.08 − 0.1 = 4.98 cm.

en.q: In a vernier callipers, 20 VSD coincide with 16 MSD (each division of length 1 mm). The least count of the vernier callipers is :
en.sol: 20 VSD = 16 MSD ⇒ 1 VSD = 0.8 mm. Least count = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = 1 − 0.8 = 0.2 mm = 0.02 cm.
